conventions.convention: The parameter dimension is positive, the parameter domain is open, candidate conditions form a finite nonempty set, observations are C1, and observation precision matrices are symmetric positive definite.

Only positive-weight conditions enter the stacked observation map and sensitivity Jacobian. Local identifiability means injectivity on an open neighborhood; global identifiability means injectivity on the entire parameter domain.
Approximate designs have nonnegative real weights summing to one; exact integer run allocation is a separate problem.
Matrix error bounds use the Euclidean operator norm. Singular values in the perturbation lemma are indexed from 1 through min(m,n).
The log-determinant perturbation bound requires a strictly positive common quadratic-form floor on the entire exact/computed matrix segment.
The multiplicative procedure uses exact arithmetic, counts weight updates with a nonnegative integer budget N, scans at indices 0 through N, and tests zero violation before budget exhaustion.
The parameter-error estimate is conditional on an existing fit inside the stated closed ball; when L=0 its radius is r0, otherwise it is min(r0, μ/(2L)).

load_bearing.statement: Local identifiability at θ0 means injectivity of the supported joint observation map on some open neighborhood of θ0. Its weighted information matrix is Mθ(ξ)=Σx ξx Jx(θ)ᵀ Wx Jx(θ).
Uniform bounds ‖Jx‖₂≤K, ‖Jh,x−Jx‖₂≤η, and ‖Wx‖₂≤w imply ‖Mh(ξ)−M(ξ)‖₂≤δ:=w(2Kη+η²) for every approximate design. A true quadratic-form floor α>δ gives computed floor α−δ.
For symmetric p×p matrices A,B with p≥1 and common segment quadratic-form floor α>0, |log det B−log det A|≤p‖B−A‖₂/α.

For the finite nonlinear observation design at a fixed parameter and approximate design, the weighted information matrix is positive definite if and only if the stacked support sensitivity Jacobian has trivial kernel, equivalently full column rank.

Starting from approximate weights with positive-definite information, every multiplicative update preserves nonnegative weights summing to one and positive definiteness. For finite budget N, the procedure returns after at most N updates and N+1 sensitivity scans.

For any returned nonsingular approximate design ξ, v=maxx fxᵀM(ξ)⁻¹fx−p is nonnegative; every nonsingular approximate competitor η satisfies log det M(η)−log det M(ξ)≤v; and v=0 if and only if ξ is D-optimal among nonsingular approximate designs.
For the C1 joint observation map on an open parameter domain of positive dimension, full column rank of its Jacobian at θ0 implies injectivity on an open neighborhood of θ0.

On the stated nonempty compact metric design space, with continuous criteria, uniform sensitivity error δ=w(2Kη+η²), and common positive segment floor α, a τ-approximate computed maximizer has true log-determinant gap at most τ+2pδ/α.

concerns.concern: The title says “Parallel first-order decay identifies only the sum of two rates”, but the permitted finite nonempty observation set may be T={0}. Then every observation equals A0 independently of k1+k2, so even the sum is not identifiable. The body correctly proves nonseparation and rank at most one; the title's positive identifiability assertion needs a positive observation time or wording that merely says observations depend only on the sum.

The remark begins “For the unweighted nonlinear least-squares objective” and asserts the exact Hessian identity without stating that the residual map is C2. Its cited supplier thm-nonlinear-least-squares-gradient-and-hessian explicitly requires C2, whereas the batch observation definition supplies only C1. For example r(θ)=1+|θ|^(3/2) is C1 but its squared-residual objective has no second derivative at zero. The intended supplier hypothesis is immediately recoverable, but should be stated in the remark.
